modules.sourceReference: Day 1 content and summary, pages 2–6; answers cross-checked with facilitator pages 10 and 32–33
modules.title: Day 1 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: Which three disciplines form the foundation of data science?
questions.explanation: The facilitator recap defines data science as the intersection of statistics, programming and domain knowledge.

questions.question: What are the four types of analytics?
questions.explanation: The four types are Descriptive, Diagnostic, Predictive and Prescriptive analytics.

options.label: Mean, Median, Mode and Standard Deviation

questions.question: Which type of analytics answers 'Why did it happen?'
questions.explanation: Diagnostic analytics investigates the factors or reasons behind past performance.

questions.question: What is the correct data science lifecycle sequence?
questions.explanation: The lifecycle is Ask, Gather, Clean, Explore, Model, Evaluate and Communicate, and it is iterative rather than strictly linear.

options.label: Ask, Gather, Clean, Explore, Model, Evaluate, Communicate
Model, Deploy, Gather, Clean, Ask, Evaluate, Archive
Plan, Budget, Build, Test, Sell, Support, Close

questions.question: How does a Data Analyst's primary focus differ from a Data Scientist's?
questions.explanation: A Data Analyst primarily explains what happened through reports and dashboards, while a Data Scientist builds models to predict what may happen.

options.label: Analysts focus on what happened; Data Scientists focus on what may happen
Analysts build hardware; Data Scientists manage networks
Analysts use no data; Data Scientists use only images
The roles always have identical responsibilities

modules.sourceReference: Day 2 content and summary, pages 7–10; answers cross-checked with facilitator pages 17 and 33
modules.title: Day 2 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: Which is an example of structured data?
questions.explanation: Structured data is organised into rows and columns, such as SQL tables, spreadsheets and CSV files.

options.label: A customer table in a SQL database

questions.question: Which list contains common data quality issues?
questions.explanation: The module highlights missing values, duplicates, inconsistent formats, outliers and typos as common quality issues.

options.label: Missing values, duplicates, inconsistent formats and outliers

questions.question: What should you do before removing an apparent outlier?
questions.explanation: Outliers should be investigated using context and domain knowledge before removal because they may be valid observations.

options.label: Investigate it and consider domain knowledge
Delete it immediately in every case
Replace it with zero without checking
Duplicate it to balance the dataset

questions.question: Which transformation combines records from different datasets?
questions.explanation: Joining combines related data from two or more datasets.

questions.question: What is the best treatment for duplicate records?
questions.explanation: Duplicates should be identified and deduplicated, retaining the first or most complete valid record according to an explicit rule.

options.label: Identify and remove duplicates using a defined retention rule
Keep every duplicate because more rows always improve analysis

modules.sourceReference: Day 3 content and summary, pages 11–13; answers cross-checked with facilitator pages 22 and 34
modules.title: Day 3 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)?
questions.explanation: EDA explores data to understand its characteristics, quality, patterns and relationships before formal modelling.

options.label: Exploring data to understand it before formal modelling
Deploying a completed model into production
Removing every unusual value from a dataset
Creating only the final executive presentation

questions.question: Which statistic is the middle value and is robust to outliers?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle ordered value and is less affected by extreme values than the mean.

questions.question: Which chart is best for showing revenue trends over time?
questions.explanation: A line chart is well suited to showing change and trends across time.

questions.question: Which chart is best for examining the relationship between ad spend and sales?
questions.explanation: A scatter plot shows the relationship between two numerical variables.

questions.question: Which is a sound data-visualisation practice?
questions.explanation: Effective visualisations use the right chart, label axes and titles, avoid clutter and use honest scales.

options.label: Label axes and titles and remove unnecessary clutter
Remove labels so the chart looks cleaner
Distort the scale to make small changes look dramatic
Use as many colours and decorations as possible

modules.sourceReference: Day 4 content and summary, pages 14–17; answers cross-checked with facilitator pages 27 and 34
modules.title: Day 4 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the difference between correlation and causation?
questions.explanation: Correlation indicates a relationship; causation means one variable produces a change in another. Correlation alone does not prove causation.

options.label: Correlation is a relationship; causation means one variable causes the other
Causation measures averages; correlation measures totals

questions.question: What does a p-value of 0.03 indicate at a 0.05 significance level?
questions.explanation: A p-value of 0.03 is below 0.05, so the result is statistically significant and the null hypothesis is rejected.

options.label: The result is statistically significant, so reject the null hypothesis
The result is not significant, so accept every alternative claim
There is a 30% probability that the data is correct

questions.question: Which machine-learning type learns from labelled data?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains on labelled examples to predict outcomes such as classes or continuous values.

questions.question: Which machine-learning approach is appropriate for grouping customers by behaviour without existing labels?
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning identifies patterns or clusters in unlabelled data; K-Means is a clustering algorithm covered in the module.

questions.question: Why should a model be evaluated on separate test data?
questions.explanation: Unseen test data provides a more honest estimate of how the model generalises beyond the examples used for training.

options.label: To measure performance on unseen data and assess generalisation
To make the training data larger
To guarantee the model has no errors
To avoid choosing an evaluation metric

modules.sourceReference: Day 5 content and summary, pages 18–21; answers cross-checked with facilitator pages 28 and 34
modules.title: Day 5 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the correct structure of a data story?
questions.explanation: The course structures a data story as Context, Data, Insight and Recommendation.

questions.question: What do executives usually care about most in a data presentation?
questions.explanation: Executives typically need the business impact and a clear recommendation rather than detailed methodology.

questions.question: Which role primarily focuses on building and maintaining data pipelines?
questions.explanation: Data Engineers focus on data pipelines and commonly use technologies such as SQL, Spark and Airflow.

questions.question: What makes a strong beginner data portfolio?
questions.explanation: The module recommends two or three varied projects using real data, with the process documented and the story clearly communicated.

options.label: A few varied real-data projects with documented process, insight and recommendation
A list of tools without any completed projects
Only screenshots with no explanation or data source
One copied project with no personal analysis

questions.question: In the churn scenario, what recommendation follows from finding that customers with more than three first-month support calls are five times more likely to churn?
questions.explanation: The facilitator answer recommends proactive outreach to high-contact customers based on the identified churn risk.

options.label: Proactively contact and support high-contact customers
Remove those customers from the dataset
Ignore the finding until every customer has churned
